messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — vanguard-liteq (int8) canary against the funcall suite is showing elevated JSON parse failures. 1.8% parse rejects vs 0.03% on fp16. Posting a couple samples and config. @sam @liam can you take a look?

sam: Thanks — paste a failing sample + canary config please.

maria: Canary config: `model=vanguard-liteq:int8`, `batch_size=8`, `kv_prefix=1024`, `retry_budget=1`, `canary=on`. Failing output (raw model text):

```
{"action": "invoke_tool", "name": "get_user", "args": {"id": 123,}

Note: there's a trailing comma after 123, and sometimes a newline inside a string: \"note:\nuser created\" which breaks our strict parser. Parser error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value at char 342.
```

liam: Ugh — trailing comma + stray newline inside string. That smells like tokenization boundary / rounding differences from quantization. Does it correlate with long prefix lengths?

maria: Yes — failures spike when prefix tokens > ~768. Short prompts (~200 tokens) are fine. We plotted fail rate vs seq len; big jump 1400-2000. Also saw a few cases of truncated closing `]` or `}` (stream cut).

nina: On previous int8 experiments we saw microquant kernel reorderings change emitted whitespace in ~0.1% of cases. If whitespace shifts, it can break strict JSON where commas/braces get split across tokens. Try disabling kv-cache and micro-pack.

sam: good idea. @canary-bot can you queue a mirror run: same traffic but kv_cache off + microquant_pack=false + retry_budget=3? We'll compare parses.

canary-bot: mirror job queued: `mirror-1799998001-1` with overrides {kv_cache:false, microquant_pack:false, retry_budget:3}. Estimated runtime 12m.

maria: I paused the staged rollout in Dedicated — not promoting from canary. Re-ran a small mirrored sample with kv_cache disabled and microquant_pack off: failures dropped to 0.05% (still above fp16 baseline). Most remaining fails are trailing commas / missing final brace.

liam: That suggests either partial-stream boundary or generation cutoff. Do we see correlation with streaming chunk size?

maria: Canary used `stream_chunk=128`. I tried `stream_chunk=256` and saw slightly fewer truncations. Also attempted `postprocess=json-healer` that heuristically fixes trailing commas and adds closing braces — healed ~70% of remaining fails.

sam: Important: do NOT roll to prod until we can get healed>90% or fallback behavior in place. If healed has to run, quantify latency cost.

nina: Also try a tokenizer-alignment test: rerun the prompt but force a one-token shift in prefix (insert harmless comment) to see if boundary moves the comma to previous token. If shifts remove fail, it's alignment problem.

maria: Good call — did a two-run A/B with a 1-token pad; fail rate almost disappeared on padded runs. Hypothesis: quantized softmax/rounding changed tokenization outputs -> punctuation emitted at token boundaries.

liam: Ok actionable list: 1) Add canary telemetry tag `canary:vanguard-liteq:int8:json-parse`. 2) Run larger mirror with kv_cache off and microquant_pack off. 3) Add tokenizer-alignment variant and collect diff heatmap. 4) If alignment explains majority, implement either small prompt padding OR run json-healer postprocess as a short-term fix.

sam: +1. Also measure healed-path latency and cost; if heal adds >15ms P99 or >3% cost maybe prefer fp16 fallback with auto-route.

maria: Agreed. I'll run the larger mirror and telemetry sweep now, attach artifacts when done. Paused canary rollout until we confirm. Link to artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/canaries/1799998001 (contains logs, heatmaps, sample outputs).

canary-bot: mirror job `mirror-1799998001-1` completed. Summary: kv_cache_off + microquant_pack_off -> parse failures down to 0.05%. Tokenizer-alignment test showed 92% of remaining fails are alignment-sensitive.

maria: Thanks all. Plan: 1) keep rollback paused, 2) add 1-token pad in the onboarding harness for int8 variants, 3) add json-healer postprocess as guardrail, 4) require healed>90% in next canary before any rollout. Filing follow-up ticket with more details. :thumbsup:

sam: Sounds good. Post results here when you have them; we may want to ship an autopatcher in the runtime to apply padding automatically for `funcall` prompts.

liam: sgtm.

maria: will do, thanks everyone.
